statement.p: Oil spilled from a ruptured tanker spreads in a circle whose area increases at a constant rate of 6 {\rm mi}^2{\rm /hr}. How rapidly is radius of the spill increasing when the area is 5 {\rm mi}^2?
The radius is increasing at mi/hr.

solution.p: The area of a circle is A=\pi r^2. So taking the derivative of both sides we get \frac{dA}{dt}=2 \pi r \frac{dr}{dt} We are looking for \frac{dr}{dt}, and we are given that \frac{dA}{dt}=6, so we need to find r. But we know that A= 5, so 5=\pi r^2 and thus r=\sqrt{\frac{5}{\pi}}=1.26157 Substituting back in to \frac{dA}{dt}=2 \pi r \frac{dr}{dt} we get 6=2\pi \cdot 1.26157 \frac{dr}{dt} and thus \frac{dr}{dt}= \frac{6}{2\pi \cdot 1.26157 }=0.75694
